# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 96 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 96 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_096_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 13

**1** I asked him, "Lord, show me also the mountain with the most verdant grass, where the animals were feeding and the birds resting." **2** "All the nations that dwell under heaven," he said, "when they heard and believed, were called by the name of the Son of God. **3** Having received the seal, they had one heart, one mind, one faith, one love, and they carried with them the spirits of the virgins. For this reason the tower appeared to be made from one stone." **4** "But what does the gate signify?" I asked. **5** "Listen," he said. "All these stones that entered the tower had to pass through the gate, and the gate is the Son of God. **6** This is the only entrance to the Lord, and no one shall enter to him otherwise than through his Son. **7** Do you see this gate? How ancient it is — yet how new! The grace given through the gate is new and fresh, and those who enter through it are blessed — those who believe and live." **8** "Why then is the gate both ancient and new?" I asked. **9** "Listen," he said. "The Son of God is more ancient than all creation, and was present as counselor at the creation of all things. **10** Therefore he is ancient. But the gate appeared new in the last days, so that those who are to be saved might enter through it into the kingdom of God. **11** Did you see that the stones that came through the gate entered the building of the tower, but those that did not come through it were returned to their own place?" **12** "I see it, Lord," I replied. "In this way also," he said, "no one shall enter the kingdom of God who does not receive the name of the Son of God. **13** For if you wish to enter a city that is walled and has only one gate, can you enter that city except through the gate it has? **14** In the same way, no one enters the kingdom of God except through the name of his Son who is beloved by him. Did you see the multitude of those who built the tower?" "I saw them, Lord."

---

### Translator's Note
This chapter's gate theology is among the richest in early Christianity: the gate is simultaneously the pre-existent Son (ancient counselor at creation, echoing Prov 8) and the eschatological entry point opened in the last days (new). The four-fold unity of v. 3 — heart, mind, faith, love — is a profound description of baptismal community. SOPHIA follows LOGOS; PNEUMA adds "baptism" as gloss in v. 3 — helpful but not in the Greek.
